title: SummitBank vendor security evidence bundle - compact packet and response notes
body:
Purpose:
This is the compact evidence bundle assembled for SummitBank’s vendor security review (POC + pilot). The packet is intentionally slimmed down for faster customer review; it references full artifacts in the S3 bucket above and the Confluence POC Hub. Use this doc as the deliverable for the security workshop and for asynchronous follow-up.

Scope and caveats:
- Scope: Hosted Redwood API (hosted inference) + Dedicated proof-of-concept cluster used during pilot. No on-prem code was delivered.
- Data: Test corpus contained synthetic PII and masked real-sample traces; we document the sampling and deletion policy below.
- Note: This packet is curated to avoid sharing full KMS keys, private certs, or full log dumps. We provide redacted extracts and verified checksums for full files.

Quick contents index (what is attached / referenced):
1) Architecture summary (attachment: architecture-onepager.pdf - redacted network diagram)
2) Logical data flow (attachment: dataflow-summary.png)
3) Configuration exports (attachments: tfstate-redwood-pilot-redacted.json, kube-config-redacted.yaml)
4) Access & Identity proofs (attachments: sso-saml-metadata.xml, okta-role-mapping.csv)
5) Encryption & key management (attachment: kms-integration-checklist.md)
6) Audit logs sample (attachment: audit-log-sample-redacted.log - 7 days)
7) Vulnerability scan summary + remediation notes (attachment: snyk-report-summary.pdf)
8) Pen test snapshot (attachment: pen-test-exec-summary-2025-10.pdf - executive summary only)
9) SOC2 mapping table (attachment: soc2-controls-mapping.csv - redacted)
10) Change history and evidence manifest (attachment: evidence-manifest.csv)

Artifact brief descriptions and why they’re included:
- architecture-onepager.pdf: single-page view of the deployed pilot with network zones, public endpoints, and the dedicated inference cluster nodes. Sensitive IPs are redacted; full export available under S3 with checksum sha256: e3b0c442... (manifest).
- dataflow-summary.png: shows request lifecycle from customer app -> API gateway -> routing layer -> serving runtime -> cache -> KMS-encrypted logging. Annotated to show PII handling and retention windows.
- tfstate-redwood-pilot-redacted.json: Terraform state export with resource names and hashes; secrets and provider tokens removed. Used to demonstrate IaC reproducibility and hardening practices.
- kube-config-redacted.yaml: cluster access config showing RBAC groups and node pools (kubelet tokens redacted).
- sso-saml-metadata.xml + okta-role-mapping.csv: evidence of SSO integration, principle of least privilege mapping for SummitBank's pilot team accounts.
- kms-integration-checklist.md: shows customer KMS key policy, envelope encryption approach (data keys rotated monthly), HSM-backed KMS usage on Dedicated nodes, and code pointers for decrypt/encrypt wrappers.
- audit-log-sample-redacted.log: chronological sample showing admin actions, model deployment events, and access requests. Sensitive fields redacted, format and retention demonstrated.
- snyk-report-summary.pdf + remediation notes: highlights low/medium findings during pilot image scans; includes ticket references and patch dates (JIRA-SEC-1389, JIRA-ENG-1476).
- pen-test-exec-summary-2025-10.pdf: vendor pen test summary focusing on the hosted control plane; no critical findings, three medium items closed during pilot. Full report available under NDA and S3.
- soc2-controls-mapping.csv: maps SummitBank’s questionnaire items to Redwood’s SOC2 controls and evidence items in this packet.

Control highlights (short answers for common questionnaire items):
- Encryption at rest: AES-256 for customer data, envelope encryption with customer-specific data keys stored in KMS. Evidence: kms-integration-checklist.md, tfstate key-policy excerpt.
- Encryption in transit: TLS 1.2+ with strong cipher suites; mutual TLS for internal service-to-service communications in Dedicated. Evidence: architecture-onepager.pdf, audit-log-sample.
- Access control: SSO enforced for console and API (Okta SAML), role-based access control for infra, ephemeral kubectl sessions via OIDC. Evidence: sso-saml-metadata.xml, okta-role-mapping.csv.
- Logging and auditability: Immutable audit logs retained for 90 days (pilot set at 30 days); exports to secure S3 with object locks available for enterprise license. Evidence: audit-log-sample-redacted.log + evidence-manifest.csv.
- Secrets management: KMS + secrets manager, scoped service identities, rotation policy documented. Evidence: kms-integration-checklist.md, tfstate redacted.
- Vulnerability management: Weekly image scans, quarterly pentests + continuous SCA. Evidence: snyk-report-summary.pdf, pen-test-exec-summary-2025-10.pdf.

Redaction and verification process used for this packet:
- Sensitive values (IP addresses, cert private keys, full log PII) were replaced with placeholders of the form <REDACTED:reason>.
- Each redacted file includes a verification checksum pointing to the full artifact in S3 (read-only, time-limited link available on request).
- Verification performed by Marcus Li (security engineer) on 2025-11-12; signature: MarcusLi-20251112.sig (stored in evidence manifest).

Open items / outstanding asks from SummitBank security team (captured during workshop):
1) Request for full SOC2 type II report (we provided summary; full attestation requires NDA and audit release). Owner: Priya -> legal. Target: 2025-11-26.
2) Confirm retention policy for pilot artifacts in S3 (customer asked for 180-day hold). Action: ops to confirm retention and object-lock feasibility. Ticket: JIRA-SEC-1432.
3) Provide encrypted log-forwarder config for centralized bank SIEM (Splunk/QRadar sample). Action: engineering to deliver sample conf and substantiation (s3 link). ETA: 2025-11-21.
4) Customer asked for additional detail on HSM provider and certs for Dedicated nodes. Action: include HSM PKI chain and vendor contact under NDA. Owner: Elena. ETA: 2025-11-19.

Workshop notes (short, verbatim-ish bullets):
- 2025-11-12 session with SummitBank infosec and infra ops (Alex Monroe, Sara Kline): live demo of dedicated cluster; walked through deployment, role separation, and SSO enrollment.
- Customer appreciated envelope encryption approach; asked for example KMS policy to present to their GRC.
- Concern raised about prefix caching: explained evict-on-expiry, no persistent storage of user prompts beyond retention window. Follow-up: short tech note attached (caching-behavior-shortnote.md).
- Asked about rollback behavior and auto-fallback to smaller model family under capacity pressure — answered with routing policy doc pointer and failover playbook.

(Full manifest attached as evidence-manifest.csv in S3)

How to validate full artifacts (for SummitBank security):
- Procedure: request time-limited S3 presigned links via our security portal (Confluence POC Hub > Evidence Access request form).
- NDA: full pentest report and SOC2 Type II only provided after signed NDA / standard AUP.
- Live validation: we offer a scheduled remote session where we can walk through the unredacted files in a shared screen with NDAs/controls in place.

Next steps and owners summary:
- Priya: coordinate NDA and send SOC2 access request (target 2025-11-19).
- Marcus: produce Splunk forwarder conf sample and upload to S3 (target 2025-11-21).
- Elena: gather HSM vendor PKI artifacts and prepare NDA redline (target 2025-11-19).
- Dev: confirm retention policy change feasibility and estimate cost delta for 180-day hold (ticket JIRA-SEC-1432).
